## Wrap values through a callback or the layout (`periodic`) {#sec-ch11-periodic}

<!-- PROVENANCE
pin: snapy@e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0
status: draft
-->

### Summary

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
Use an in-block opposite-side copy when a callback remains, or a wrapped neighbour exchange when the layout owns periodicity.
Default: off; external faces default reflecting.
Order: exact discrete operation or local derivation below; coupled solver order not measured.
:::

### Derivation

For a periodic field, translation by the domain length leaves its cell integral unchanged. On matched
cells the discrete boundary operation is therefore an exact permutation of cell averages, not an interpolation.
With owned cells $1,\ldots,n_1$ and ghost depth $l$, the x1 callback gives

$$
\begin{aligned}
q_{1-l}&=q_{n_1+1-l},\\
q_{n_1+l}&=q_l.
\end{aligned}
$$ {#eq-ch11-periodic-copy}

`periodic_inner` and `periodic_outer` ([`bc_func.cpp:36-50`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/bc/bc_func.cpp#L36-L50)) implement @eq-ch11-periodic-copy.
For several blocks, the donor is the wrapped neighbour selected by `neighbor_rank` ([`slab_layout.cpp:41-70`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/layout/slab_layout.cpp#L41-L70)), and the same
identity applies to the global cell index. This proves exact copying on a matching periodic mesh, not the
conservation of independently reconstructed seam fluxes. C1 checks both callback copies and repeated fills.

The report-only checks are `src/snapy_report/ch11/boundary_check.py`; their current output is
`src/snapy_report/ch11/boundary_check.out`. They do not call a snapy kernel.

### Numerical method

The layout flag `periodic_x` refers to x2, `periodic_y` to x3, and `periodic_z` to x1. YAML sets the first
two for periodic x2/x3; x1 sets the layout flag only for layout type `cubed`. A slab x1 periodic callback
therefore copies inside the block. Layout-owned wraps have null callbacks and are filled at exchange time.
No independent convergence order is associated with this exact permutation.

@fig-ch11-periodic-stencil illustrates the operations, with labelled roles independent of colour.

```{python}

#| fig-cap: "Wrap values through a callback or the layout. Schematic only; no simulation measurements."
#| fig-alt: "Labelled schematic of the periodic boundary operation; ghosts and owned cells have separate text labels."
```

1. Parse periodic face names and set the appropriate layout flag. The anchor `periodic_x` is in [`meshblock_options.cpp:139-201`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/mesh/meshblock_options.cpp#L139-L201).
2. Null layout-owned face callbacks; retain the x1 slab callback. The anchor `bfuncs` is in [`meshblock.cpp:138-166`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/mesh/meshblock.cpp#L138-L166).
3. Copy the opposite owned slab or obtain the wrapped neighbour through the layout. The anchor `periodic_inner` is in [`bc_func.cpp:36-50`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/bc/bc_func.cpp#L36-L50).

### Limits

::: {.callout-warning title="Limits"}
In-block copy and neighbour exchange are distinct paths. The outline also inventories the multi-rank
exchange and positivity seam suites; their runtime coverage remains pending in @sec-ch15-ch11. A copied donor
factor must stay single-valued across its shared face; this section does not replace the positivity analysis.

Untested switch combinations remain subject to @sec-ch12-matrix. No new CPU, CUDA or multi-rank solver result is claimed.
:::
